title: Nether Beast Character Study: Devotee plus Demotee equals 2 Timothy (4_3)
summary: Part four of NH's character study mocking former fitness YouTuber Nether Beast, whom he calls a pathological liar and grandiose narcissist on par with another fitness personality. He answers a fan's criticism, then ridicules Nether's fitness claims, fighting excuses, bad advice and a story about aliens fixing his clavicle.
claims: Fanboyism toward fitness personalities is like a mental illness and blinds followers to obvious lies
Many viewers drift from fitness guru to guru looking for a new messiah; some left his channel when he refused to be that figure
He says he never uses names, clickbait or name drops in titles; the character studies get about a thousand views while his ab video got 50k
A former fitness YouTuber now recycles thumbnails from his steroid days at 230-240 lb to attract viewers while being skinny now
Progress updates made from small, zoomed, blurry or old photos instead of video are a sign of deception
Rapid regrowth after losing mass is not realistic without steroids for someone who does not know how to train
Attaching 10 lb ankle weights for sprints to build hamstrings is terrible advice: it ruins sprint form and strains knee and ankle tendons and risks hamstring tears
A homemade punching tower placed away from the feet prevents hip rotation into punches, so it has no carryover to fighting
Fight records matter; a fighter with more losses than wins is a bad fighter, and dismissing records is a coping mechanism
Neck hair is not evidence of high testosterone; bragging about high testosterone is pointless if it doesn't translate into muscle
He boxed and got beaten by smaller opponents, which he used as a lesson rather than dismissing the sport
Gloved boxing raises long-term concussion risk, but bare-knuckle fighting was abandoned for good reasons like eye loss and facial nerve damage
